teaching_point: Mild erythematotelangiectatic phenotype: persistent centrofacial erythema with fine telangiectasia. This is the Day 1 case pattern (35-year-old, flushing with pepper and wine, now persistent).

teaching_point: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea on the convex face (nose, cheeks, chin). Periocular sparing helps separate it from SLE and dermatomyositis. No comedones.
dermnet_caption: Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea on the nose cheeks and chin
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea on the nose cheeks and chin (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/rosacea-images

teaching_point: Transient flushing (the early phase). A trigger diary helps (heat, alcohol, spicy food, hot drinks, sun, exercise). Red flags for another cause: wheeze, diarrhoea, palpitations, sweating (carcinoid, mastocytosis, phaeochromocytoma, menopause, drugs).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Rosacea causing flushing (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/flushing

teaching_point: Papulopustular phenotype on the cheeks: dome-shaped papules and pustules on background erythema, with NO comedones. First line is topical ivermectin 1% (CKS).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papular rosacea on the cheeks (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/rosacea-images

teaching_point: Moderate papulopustular rosacea: consider topical ivermectin plus doxycycline 40 mg MR. Review at 8–12 weeks and taper to topical maintenance.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papulopustular rosacea on the cheek (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/rosacea-images

teaching_point: Severe papulopustular rosacea with early rhinophyma: oral tetracycline plus topical. Refer if refractory (specialists may use low-dose isotretinoin off-label).
dermnet_caption: Severe papulopustular rosacea with a rhinophyma
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Severe papulopustular rosacea with a rhinophyma (© Dr Lawrence Meyerson) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/rosacea-images

teaching_point: Phymatous change (rhinophyma), mostly in men. This alone is diagnostic of rosacea (2017 phenotype criteria). Treatment is surgical, laser or ablative; NHS funding is variable.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Papulopustular and ocular rosacea together. Up to half of rosacea patients have eye symptoms, and these can come before the skin signs. Always ask about grittiness or dryness.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papulopustular and ocular rosacea (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/rosacea-images

teaching_point: Ocular rosacea: lid-margin telangiectasia, blepharitis, meibomian gland dysfunction. Treat with lid hygiene and warm compresses (± oral tetracycline). SAME-DAY eye referral for pain, photophobia or reduced vision (keratitis).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Granulomatous rosacea: firm yellow-brown monomorphic papules, which can be periocular. DDx: sarcoid, lupus miliaris, granulomatous periorificial dermatitis. Biopsy or refer if unsure.
dermnet_caption: Granulomatous rosacea and rosacea eye disease
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Granulomatous rosacea and rosacea eye disease (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/rosacea-images

teaching_point: Demodicosis: fine follicular scale ('frosting', 'nutmeg-grater' texture) with small papulopustules. Itch or burn more than flushing. Demodex density is high and responds to ivermectin or permethrin.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)

teaching_point: Rosacea-like demodicosis (Day 2 Demodex question): consider it when 'rosacea' is asymmetric, scaly, or flared by topical steroid/immunosuppression. The ivermectin response supports the mite's role.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Rosacea due to demodicosis (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/demodex

teaching_point: Dermoscopy of demodicosis: 'Demodex tails' (whitish gelatinous threads) and follicular plugs. Standardised skin-surface biopsy (more than 5 mites/cm²) is a specialist test.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy of demodicosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/demodex

teaching_point: Steroid-induced rosacea: erythema, telangiectasia and papulopustules after facial TCS (often OTC hydrocortisone or 'lightening' creams). Stop the TCS (warn of rebound), then use metronidazole/azelaic acid or an oral tetracycline.
dermnet_caption: Steroid induced rosacea on the forehead
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Steroid induced rosacea on the forehead (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/rosacea

teaching_point: Swelling and papulopustules in steroid rosacea. Withdrawal causes a predictable flare over 1–3 weeks, so taper potent steroids if needed and give a doxycycline cover course.
dermnet_caption: Swelling and papulopustules in steroid induced rosacea
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Swelling and papulopustules in steroid induced rosacea (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/rosacea

teaching_point: DDx periorificial dermatitis: perioral/nasolabial papules with a SPARED rim next to the vermilion, often in young women using TCS or heavy creams ('zero therapy' first). Module 4 exam Q25.
dermnet_caption: Perioral erythematous papules sparing the immediate perivermillion skin in perioral dermatitis
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
